steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Comparing requires identifying both similarities and differences — not just one or the other

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Use linking words: 'similarly', 'in contrast', 'whereas', 'both', 'however' to show comparison clearly

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Always compare the same element — for example, compare use of dynamics in both works

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evaluating means making a judgement about effectiveness, supported by specific evidence

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the key difference between comparing and evaluating dance? | Q: Name three linking words that help structure a comparison answer. | Q: What criteria could you use to evaluate the effectiveness of a choreographic work?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Comparing identifies similarities and differences between works. Evaluating goes further by making a judgement about effectiveness, weighing evidence to reach a supported conclusion about quality or i | Similarly, in contrast, whereas. These signal to the examiner that you are making direct comparisons rather than writing about each work separately. | Clarity of intention, audience impact, technical execution, use of choreographic devices, structure, creativity and how well movement communicates meaning are all valid evaluation criteria.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Plan comparison answers in a table before writing — list similarities and differences for each element Never write about one work then the other separately — interleave your points with linking words For evaluation, introduce your criteria early so the examiner knows your basis for judgement Support every comparative point with at least one specific example from each work In evaluation answers, always finish with a clear, one-sentence judgement that answers the question
